caveats: Same charged work holds to 1.7e-6 (24 bits), 3.2e-7 (28) and 3.8e-8 (32), not exactly. dg charges one extra GAE for each repeated target its deferred guard catches after decomposition (repeated_targets_skipped): 20, 24 and 19 of 288 pairs, +22, +24 and +20 GAE in total, never fewer than srenew. Section 6.1 condition 8 (|ratio - 1| < 0.0005 at w = 0) holds. Consequence: dg and srenew are not ordered in counted units across the section 5a band (srenew lower at w = 0 on every curve, dg lower at w = 0.1 and 1). The admitted improvement is wall-clock per charged GAE only. The counted headline S is unchanged at w = 0 to within 2e-6.

ns per GAE is an upper bound on the cost per operation for both arms, since both carry unpriced native work. The ratio is wall per charged GAE on one host class (EKS c8a.2xlarge, env class ECBENV3hc1c5e5126853).

Wall time cannot be replayed. The replay certificate covers counted scalars only. The wall statistic rests on four things: in-job L2 grading of all 1,680 executions per wall session, native A/A admission (control-comparison.json), the srenew/srenew-aa A/A at 0.9998, 0.99994 and 0.9987 (intervals contain 1), and the validator's recompute.

Order confound, checked. Under the frozen 'alternate' order, dg ran at position 2 of the 5-run block in all 288 blocks; srenew and srenew-aa ran at positions 1 and 3. The A/A therefore cannot detect a position-2 effect. Within-run null objects bound one: the oracle_setup phase does identical work in the same process and position, and its wall ratio dg/srenew is 1.0016, 0.9985 and 0.9994. Against that, the relations phase ratio is 0.870, 0.834 and 0.793, and it carries 98.6-102% of the solve-wall saving. The per-pair saving tracks removed guard probes (r = 0.89, 0.90, 0.93) with a negative intercept. The A/A difference does not track them (r = -0.0001, -0.016, 0.092).

Two curves per size. The per-curve corrected ratios differ between the two curves beyond their intervals at 24 bits (0.907 vs 0.920) and 32 bits (0.865 vs 0.836). The pooled interval therefore describes these two curves, not curves in general. The target-clustered intervals are close to the frozen pair interval; at 32 bits it is wider ([0.8433, 0.8539] against [0.8451, 0.8521]). Every upper bound is below 1.
With the A/A including arm A over the same 288 pairs, the corrected ratio equals ns(dg) / ns(srenew-aa) exactly. The independent-error combination counts srenew's noise twice and is conservative.

Memory alongside time. dg's mean max RSS is lower at 32 bits (96,243 to 80,383 KiB) and its mean minor faults in the solve are lower at every size (366 to 265, 2,085 to 1,430, 16,288 to 10,529). Part of the saving is the guard table's memory work. That is executed native work, not accounting.

28 bits: E6 condition 2 fails on both curves (sum total_gae dg - srenew = +12 on each curve), so srenew stays the 28-bit baseline, as the producer reports. The protocol places only a 24/32-bit component speed-up and a 28-bit baseline change. A 28-bit component speed-up row is not specified, so that placement is the Coordinator's decision.

limitations: The measurement and the replay used the same binary (88070375), because no other binary contains these targets; the replay host (Intel Xeon @ 2.1 GHz, 4 CPUs) differs from the measuring pods. The implementation-independent checks are the validator's stdlib recompute and [d]G = Q on all 12,072 records.

The frozen interval (linearised t over 288 pairs) treats pairs as independent although they are 48 targets x 6 rounds. The target-clustered linearised and bootstrap intervals (10,000 resamples, seed 20261029) are descriptive and decide nothing.
Counted-session rho executions graded L1 because the solve was under the 1 ms grading floor: 672 at 24 bits, 269 at 28 and 15 at 32. Their counts are used; their wall time is not.

predictions_vs_measured.reading: The gain at 28 and 32 bits is larger than predicted. The model weighted the guard's share by the relation phase's GAE share (0.48); the relation phase carries 0.68-0.73 of srenew's solve wall. Its own wall ratio dg/srenew (0.870, 0.834, 0.793) is a 13-21% saving inside the phase. The implied saving per removed probe, 18.7, 24.9 and 37.6 ns by totals (per-pair slope 22.4, 30.0 and 52.3 ns), is below the model's 55-70 ns and grows with the guard table, as the protocol's cache model-risk note anticipates. Descriptive only.
